why: B's migration is the one that actually works out of the box — it fixes the anthropic-1.13 TypeError and ports the n=5 reviewer ensemble inside the migration, so the default Claude run and the app's second-largest consumer both route, with every claimed site verified; A leaves both on branches, so its shipped migration still produces zero traffic on the default --model path and keeps the ensemble on OpenAI, and its m2 'live 200 for claude-3-5-sonnet with temperature 0.75' sits awkwardly against its own i3 finding that that exact call raises TypeError before any HTTP request on that branch. On system judgment B is deeper on this app specifically: it recognises that Router's levers (fallbacks, provider_timeout, allow_flex_tier, usage.cost) are Responses-only and therefore that the default Claude path on /v1/messages gets none of them (i3), and it finds the single best lever for an unattended batch job — Flex on a Flex-eligible reviewer model, measured -50% with no latency cost — which A never mentions at all.
A_best: i1, labelling requests per pipeline stage rather than per helper function, correctly identified as the enabler that turns per-stage model choice, cache keys and timeouts into one-line policy edits — the one real insight B missed; it also shipped prompt_cache_key in the migration itself, where this app's long fixed prefixes pay and nothing behavioural changes.
B_best: Spotting that Router's differentiating fields are Responses-only, so the app's default Claude model on /v1/messages gets no fallbacks, no provider_timeout, no spend label and no usage.cost — then proposing both the port (i3) and the Flex-eligible reviewer (i5, the cheapest correct lever for work no human waits on), with the honest caveat that the README's reviewer-agreement numbers must be re-measured.
A_worst: The shipped migration routes less than it reads: the default Claude model still dies with TypeError, the five-review ensemble and the ICLR benchmark's 500-paper review load stay on OpenAI, six of its claimed sites are unverified by the outside check, and it records gpt-4o-2024-05-13 -> gpt-4o as 'no change' in price when that remap is actually a 50% input cut.
B_worst: It bundled a trade-off into the migration branch — the ensemble fan-out adds ~$0.25 of input per 5-review ensemble and changes the statistics of a calibrated component — while leaving the pure-win prompt_cache_key that offsets it on a separate branch, so the migration as merged costs more per paper than it needs to; m6's edit to AVAILABLE_LLMS is also scope creep for a behaviour-preserving move.
